findings.title: WriteAll ignores the error from f.Close()
findings.detail: Unlike a read-only close, a failed close after writes can silently drop buffered data that was never flushed to disk.
findings.risk_rationale: A failed close after writing can silently lose data.

findings.title: ReadAll still ignores the error from f.Close()
findings.detail: f.Close()'s return value is discarded, so a failed close after reading raises no error to the caller.
findings.risk_rationale: A close failure on this path is silently dropped instead of surfacing to the caller.

summary: WriteAll's ignored Close error is real here, unlike ReadAll's. ReadAll's own point still stands, already dismissed.
